headline: Govt raises bus and minibus fares by Tk 0.17 per km after fuel hike
summary: The new rates apply to diesel-powered vehicles across Dhaka, Chattogram, and several other districts, while gas-powered buses remain unchanged.
details: The government has increased the fares for diesel-powered buses and minibuses by 17 paisa per kilometer following a rise in fuel prices. A gazette notification signed by Assistant Secretary Md. Jasim Uddin of the Road Transport and Highways Division was issued on Tuesday.
caption:
Bus fares are going up. Diesel-powered buses and minibuses will now cost 17 paisa more per kilometer.

The government has increased the fares for diesel-powered buses and minibuses by 17 paisa per kilometer following a rise in fuel prices. A gazette notification signed by Assistant Secretary Md. Jasim Uddin of the Road Transport and Highways Division was issued on Tuesday.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[unveils five-point plan to end Rohingya displacement]] at UN
headline: PM Tarique Rahman unveils five-point plan to end Rohingya displacement at UN
summary: The Prime Minister proposed a clear roadmap for safe, voluntary, and dignified repatriation to Myanmar, urging the international community to move from promises to effective action.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman proposed five urgent steps to resolve the long-standing Rohingya crisis during a high-level meeting at the UN headquarters in New York on Wednesday.
He urged the international community to shift from expressing sympathy to finding root causes, from promises to effective action, and from managing displacement to ending it.
The five-point plan includes creating a clear and credible roadmap for the rapid, safe, voluntary, and dignified repatriation of Rohingya people to Myanmar.
He also called for an end to violence against civilians, including the Rohingya, and the assurance of their basic rights and security in their home country.
The Prime Minister emphasized the need for adequate and predictable humanitarian assistance for both the Rohingya refugees and the host communities in Bangladesh.
Furthermore, he called for strengthened justice and accountability mechanisms to address the crimes committed against the Rohingya.
The final point of his proposal focuses on enhancing regional and international cooperation to combat cross-border crimes, including drug-based economies, human trafficking, and digital fraud.
The meeting took place in the UN conference room, where the Prime Minister discussed these proposals with the wysoklevel officials and the UNHCR chief.
caption:
From promises to action: PM Tarique Rahman proposes a 5-point plan at the UN to end the Rohingya crisis.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman proposed five urgent steps to resolve the long-standing Rohingya crisis during a high-level meeting at the UN headquarters in New York on Wednesday.

He urged the international community to shift from expressing sympathy to finding root causes, from promises to effective action, and from managing displacement to ending it.

The five-point plan includes creating a clear and credible roadmap for the rapid, safe, voluntary, and dignified repatriation of Rohingya people to Myanmar.

He also called for an end to violence against civilians, including the Rohingya, and the assurance of their basic rights and security in their home country.

The Prime Minister emphasized the need for adequate and predictable humanitarian assistance for both the Rohingya refugees and the host communities in Bangladesh.

Furthermore, he called for strengthened justice and accountability mechanisms to address the crimes committed against the Rohingya.

The final point of his proposal focuses on enhancing regional and international cooperation to combat cross-border crimes, including drug-based economies, human trafficking, and digital fraud.

The meeting took place in the UN conference room, where the Prime Minister discussed these proposals with the wysoklevel officials and the UNHCR chief.
